lawyer:
Kazi A.T. Monowaruddin with Mahbub Sobhan, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner.  

A.K.M. Shafiqur Rahman, Shahabuddin Foiz with Mostafa Kamal Pasha Advocates ----- For the O.P. No.1.
parties:
Pubali Bank Ltd ------Petitioner
vs.
Mohammed Mia & Ors ------Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Latifur Rahman, J: - This Rule at the instance of the claimant-petitioner, Pubali Bank Limited is directed against order No. 50 dated 26.2.1986 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong in Miscellaneous Judicial Case No. 108 of 1984 dismissing the said Miscellaneous Case Under Order 38 Rule 8 and 10 read with Order 21 Rule 58 and 60 of the Code of Civil Procedure for investigation and release of the attached property. 

 The petitioner, a Banking company in usual course of banking business granted credit facilities to opposite party No. 2 Messers Janapat Enterprise upto a limit of some U.S. Dollars as per terms and conditions as contained in the letter of sanction dated 11.1.1982 for the import of a Vessel M.V. Silver Port and the said vessel was beached at the ship breaking yard and was placed at the control and custody of the petitioner as the pledgee. Inspite of repeated demands by the petitioner, the Opposite parties neglected in repayment of the loan which stood at Taka 27, 24,096.13 as on 3.4.1986. In order to reduce the outstanding loan of the Opposite parties, the petitioner decided to dispose of the pledged scrapped materials through auction and took steps for sale of the pledged scraps. In the meanwhile the opposite party No. 1 (Mr. Mohammad Miah) as plaintiff filed a suit being Money Suit No.137 of 1983 on 24.11.1983 and on the same date an application for attachment before judgment was filed under Order 38 Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure. An ad interim order of attachment before judgment was passed on the same day and consequently, the auction as proposed by the petitioner could not be held. Thereafter, the petitioner as claimant filed the application on 8.1.1984 for vacating/modifying the order of attachment in Money Suit No. 137 of 1983. In the meanwhile the said money suit was decreed exparte in favour of the Opposite party No. 1 on 29.5.1984 and the Opposite party No. 1 started the Money execution case for realisation of the decrial dues by sale of the scraps of the vessel. The said application or the petitioner for vacating the order of attachment was dismissed by the Trial Court holding that the same is not maintainable and against that order the present petitioner moved this Court in Civil Revision No. 206 of 1984 wherein it was held by this Court that the Court erred in law in holding that the application under Order 38 Rule 8 of the Code for modification of the order is not maintainable and this Court directed for disposal of the macro on merit. The trial Court thereafter considered the matter on merit and passed the impugned order. 

 5. Mr. Kazi A.T. Monowaruddin, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the Trial Court on a wrong assumption of fact held that the vessel was pledged but not the scraps of the vessel and thereby the Trial Court came to a wrong finding of fact in the present case. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that from the documents as filed in the case it is proved beyond doubt that the pledged goods were in the possession of the Bank and under the law in possession may be actual, constructive and symbolical and the court failed to consider this aspect in proper connotation and consequently arrived at an erroneous decision in the case. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that the Vessels or for that matter it's scraps being pledged with the Bank, the Bank as creditors, in case of default may sell the goods after a reasonable notice as contemplated under contract Act. 

 6. Mr. A.K.M. Shafiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the Opposite party No. 1 submits that delivery of possession is essential to constitute a valid pledge and the court having found that pledged goods were not in possession of the Bank, the order of the learned Subordinate Judge suffers from no illegality and as such the same need not be set aside in the revisional jurisdiction of this Court. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 in order to get the service charges from the defendants has obtained an ex parte decree in a money suit and as such the order of investigation and release of the attached property has been rightly rejected in the case. 

 7. Heard the learned Advocates and perused the impugned order and the relevant documents filed by the parties in the case. It is not disputed before us that in course of usual banking business, the petitioner granted the credit facilities to the Opposite parties and the relevant documents were executed by the parties to the contract. We will refer here-below some of the documents to show the nature of transaction and as to how after the vessel was brought in, the parties proceeded in the matter. The relevant documents namely, Exhibit-4, photo copy of the pledge of goods, Exhibit 5 (a) authorisation letter of Opposite party No.3 to the Manager, Pubali Bank, Agra- bad Branch, Chittagong, Exhibit-7 series delivery order of the petitioner Bank in favour of Opposite party No. 2, Exhibit-8 series tender notice, Exhibit-9 delivery certificate, will show that the M.V. Silver Port was pledged with the bank and the Officer of the Bank also testified to the effect and as such there was no dispute that the vessel was pledged. 

 10. With regard to the next point of the learned Advocate for the petitioner, it is to be stated that in case of pledge normally the possession remains with the creditor and the possession may be actual/ constructive and symbolic and in the present case from exhibits 5 and 7 series it is abundantly clear that the scraps of the vessel were taken out from time to time by the authorised agents of the opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 from the petitioner Bank and as such on that score as well Mr. Kazi A.T. Monowaruddin the learned Advocate for the petitioner has rightly contended that the constructive possession of the Vessel or for that matter the scraps of the vessel were with the bank. Here we may refer that normally in Railway transaction the Railway documents and endorsement of Railway receipts have been construed in several cases as possession with the creditor. Thus, the learned Advocate has been able to substantiate that the possession was the bank and from time to time the scraps of the vessel were taken out by the Opposite parties. Thus it cannot be said that the possession of the Vessel was not with the petitioner bank. Mr. Kazi A.T. Monowaruddin, the learned Advocate further submits that the bank has got a right to sell the pledged goods by giving a reasonable notice as contemplated under the Contract Act. The learned Subordinate Judge has also found fault with the petitioner bank for not taking any steps against the defendants-opposite parties. It is to be stated here that in case of default the bank may either bring a suit or sell the pledged property after reasonable notices and for that collusion between the petitioner and the defendants-opposite parties cannot be presumed and as a matter of fact there is nothing on record to show the case of collusion between the Bank and O.P. 2 & 3. 

 11. In an application for investigation and release of the attached property under Order 28, Rule 8 read with Order 21, Rule 58 and 60 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the Court is fully competent to decide the question of the claimant and in this case we held that the learned Subordinate Judge has failed to decide that on proper interpretation of law and fact in the present case. 

 12. Mr. A.K.M. Shafiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate's contention that possession was not with the bank is untenable as we have already held earlier that the possession is an essential condition for a valid pledge and the possession was with the bank and from time to time on valid authorisation letters from the defendants, the scraps of the vessel were taken from the custody of the bank and as such the submission of the learned Advocate for the Opposite party fails. It is true that the plaintiff has filed the suit for his service charges and has obtained an ex-parte decree but that is not very relevant for investigation of the claim of the claimant-petitioner in the present proceeding. Mr. A.K.M. Shafiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate by way of an analogy stated that a cow may be pledged but if subsequently a calf is born then the calf cannot be subject-matter of pledge. We are afraid that this analogy is not legally tenable because at the time when the contract was entered into the parties knew that the vessel was pledged for the purpose of scrapings. The learned Advocate has also stated that the calf is not and cannot be subject-matter of pledge because the parties knew that the cow was not pledged. This analogy is not applicable in the case of the ship. Mr. Shafiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate's further contention that for the service charge of scrapping of the ship if the attachment order is vacated then the decree that his client has got will be frustrated as the opposite parties have got no other tangible property. In this proceeding we are only to see whether the claimant- petitioner has been able to make out a case for release of the property from attachment as he has prior claim over the pledged goods under the contract. In that view, we do not find any substance in the contention of the learned Advocate for the Opposite party. The case of Abdul Hadi Versus Maung Tun Kyaing reported in A.I.R. 1931 (Rangoon) 201 has been cited by the learned Advocate for the opposite party. That was a case of mortgage of a moveable property under Section 178 of the Contract Act and that has got no application in the facts of the present case. The learned Advocate for the Opposite party has also raised a point with regard to the notice. This is also not very material because the proceeding is primarily with regard to the investigation of the claim of the claimant. Be that as it may, the bank has made public advertisements and in the facts of the case it is to be presumed to be a reasonable notice for auction and in fact from the record we find the auction was stopped due to the proceeding between the parties and the parties knew about the matter. Thus this point is also of no substance. Consequently, the impugned order is set aside. This Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The order of attachment is vacated and the scraps of the Vessel M.V. Silver Port are released from the order of attachment. Let the money execution case No. 56 of 1984 relating to the attached property be struck off.
